messages.subject: more on K distributions
parts:
The Wikipedia article

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-distribution

is very confusing because their density function uses two parameters
(nu and L), but they also include a mean parameter mu which appears on the
right-hand side of the density definition but not the left. It looks
like everyone else is just taking mu = 1.

There's an approximation that might work here:

http://www.london-research-and-development.com/K-Distribution%20Algorithm.Version2.pdf

It's a bit of algebra, but shouldn't be hard to code in Stan.

There's also a definition in terms of an exponential and
a gamma provided here:

http://reference.wolfram.com/mathematica/ref/KDistribution.html

under "properties and relations" which is:

v ~ Gamma(nu, L/nu)

u ~ Exponential(1)

---> sqrt(u * v) ~ K(nu, L)

There's also a simple compound gamma-Rayleigh distribution. They
don't list a gamma-gamma compound distribution, nor did anything else
I saw.

- Bob
